text: While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab.
These women invited the people to the sacrifices offered to their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
So Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD's anger burned against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and impale them before the LORD in the open sunlight, so that the LORD's burning anger may turn away from Israel."

versions.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and execute them in broad daylight before the LORD, so that the LORD's burning anger may turn away from Israel."
versions.explanation: The verb הוֹקַע denotes public impalement or exposure of the body, not simply execution; the point is the public display. Also, the Hebrew places "before the LORD" before "in the sunlight," which reads more naturally aloud in that order.

text: So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you put to death the men under you who have yoked themselves to Baal of Peor."
Just then an Israelite man came and brought a Midianite woman to his family, in full view of Moses and the whole assembly of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the assembly, took a spear in his hand,
followed the Israelite into the inner chamber, and drove the spear through both of them—the Israelite man and the woman, through her body. Then the plague against the Israelites was stopped.
Those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.

versions.text: But twenty-four thousand had died in the plague.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is a simple summary statement without an adversative conjunction; "But" adds a contrast not present, and the pluperfect "had died" is unnecessary. A straightforward statement reads better for oral delivery.

text: "Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the Israelites, for he was zealous with my own zeal among them; so I did not put an end to the Israelites in my zeal.

versions.text: "Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the Israelites. Since he was as zealous for my honor among them as I am, I did not put an end to the Israelites in my zeal.
versions.explanation: "as zealous for my honor among them as I am" adds a comparison and the word "honor" that are not in the Hebrew, which reads "in that he was zealous with my zeal among them." A closer rendering also flows better and keeps the connection to the following clause.

text: Therefore say: I am giving him my covenant of peace.
It will be a covenant of a lasting priesthood for him and his descendants after him, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites."
The name of the Israelite who was killed along with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a family within the tribe of Simeon.
And the name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a family in Midian.
"Treat the Midianites as enemies and strike them down,

because they treated you as enemies when they deceived you in the affair of Peor, and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, their own sister, who was killed on the day the plague came because of Peor."
